newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov says education special session unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov says education special session unlikely.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar said he would not ask lawmakers to reconsider his education financing plan in a special session without a consensus agreement first.
"I don't think there is any reason to have a special session and waste taxpayer's money unless there's some type of a consensus," Edgar told reporters.
"I'm not going to call a session on a hope," Edgar said.
Edgar's proposed tax swap plan passed the Illinois House late last week, but died in a Senate committee a day before lawmakers adjourned their session.
The Edgar plan called for a 25 percent income tax hike to generate approximately $600 million of new revenue for elementary and secondary schools and $900 million of property tax cuts.
It also called for using $100 million of new revenue growth to finance $2 billion of school construction bonds that would be offered to local districts on a matching basis.
Illinois lawmakers approved a $342 million increase for elementary and secondary schools for fiscal 1998 in the session just concluded, according to the state budget bureau.
